inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' own currency: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% (country risk embedded), beta ~1.0 for an HK-listed China specialty pharma with policy exposure -> cost of equity ~8.8-9.0%. Net cash, so WACC ~= cost of equity: 9.0%. Used in ALL three scenarios -- VBP/NRDL policy risk, licensing-renewal risk and the tax-clawback precedent are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Lease liabilities are immaterial (RMB48.3m at 30 Jun 2026). Full lease payment (FY2025 principal RMB18,961k + interest RMB2,734k = RMB21.7m, 0.26% of revenue) charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities EXCLUDED from total_debt (bank borrowings only); da_pct_path excludes right-of-use depreciation (RMB20.6m) so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI (RMB132.4m at 30 Jun 2026, loss-making subsidiaries incl. the Dermavon/ international ventures) deducted once in the equity bridge at book; flows are modelled on the consolidated operating P&L. FY0 tie: FY2025 operating EBIT 1,641.7 x (1-22%) = 1,280.5 NOPAT; add back stripped non-operating items (associates 242.3, FVTPL fair-value gain 231.0 + dividends 32.1, interest 82.3 after tax) reconciles to the company's normalized profit of RMB1,775.5m within ~5%.
inputs.ebitda_basis: HK-format P&L has no operating-profit subtotal, so EBITDA is built from lines: Gross profit + government subsidies (Other income ex interest) - Selling - Administrative - R&D expenses, EXCLUDING Other gains and losses (FVTPL fair-value moves, FX, disposal gains), share of associates/JV, finance costs and interest income. FY2025: 5,871.5 + 63.3 - 2,842.3 - 865.8 - 585.0 = 1,641.7 EBIT; + D&A 266.9 (amortisation 199.1, PPE dep 47.2, ROU dep 20.6) = 1,908.6 EBITDA (23.2%); + SBC 27.3 = 1,935.9 adjusted EBITDA (23.6%). H1 FY2026 on the same basis ~27.4% (H1 FY2025 25.2%, H2 FY2025 21.4% on the R&D step-up), so FY2026 anchors at 25.0%. Pre-VBP years (FY2017-22) ran ~40%+ EBITDA margins on net margins of 31-36%; those are not the base -- the VBP reset plus the deliberate R&D step-up (expensed R&D 585m FY2025 vs 115m FY2021) is structural.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margins and reinvestment still normalising; terminal-year owner-FCF margin ~15% is flat). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating company (specialty pharma licensing/promotion), non-US filer -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (currency a1/a2, leases b, NCI c, matching-asset rule d). KEY JUDGMENT -- in-licensing spend IS capex: the company's 'Deposits paid for acquisition of intangible assets' (RMB473.4m FY2025, 423.3m FY2024 incl. 114.7m direct purchases, 468.1m in H1 FY2026 alone) buys the exclusive product/distribution rights that ARE the revenue base; management itself reports them as the capitalised half of 'total R&D expenditure' (FY2025: 1,058.4 = 585.0 expensed + 473.4 capitalised). Rights are finite-life (amortised 199m/yr and rising) and the VBP episode shows how fast an un-refreshed portfolio erodes, so this is maintenance-plus-growth reinvestment, not optional M&A. It is deducted every year via capex_pct_path (PPE ~0.5% + licensing 7.5% in FY2026 fading to 4.5%), and in the owner-FCF history: last_fcf 216.7 = reported FCF 717.4 - SBC 27.3 - licensing deposits 473.4. Interest income: interest received (RMB82.3m) is classified in INVESTING activities by this filer, so reported OCF/FCF already exclude it -- interest_income is set to 0 to avoid stripping it twice; the cash pile is credited once via net cash. Owner-FCF margin FY2025 was 2.6% because of a RMB650m working-capital build (trade receivables +447m, due from associates +164m on +743m revenue); wc_capture_pct is set strongly NEGATIVE (-35% base) because receivables + inventory (RMB3.2bn) far exceed payables (RMB0.3bn) -- growth consumes cash here, and DSOs have been lengthening (a watch item). Non-operating portfolio (matching-asset rule): share of associates, FVTPL gains/dividends and interest income are all stripped from the flows, so their source assets enter the equity_bridge -- associates + JV at book, FVTPL at fair value less a 20% Level-3 haircut (unlisted capital funds and biotech equity valued by management), FVTOCI at fair value, loan receivable and non-trade associate deposit at book. Those bridge items are ~RMB2.8/share (~HK$3.3) -- about a third of the value; a reader who distrusts the investment portfolio should haircut there. SBC is tiny (0.33% of revenue), so house and street nearly coincide. FY2025 reported profit fell 10.5% on a one-off RMB278.8m repayment of a 2022-24 local tax concession (incl. surcharge); the cash tax rate is set at 22% (vs 25% PRC statutory, ~20.5% normalized FY2025 ETR on operating profit) because the concession is gone and PRC dividend withholding applies on repatriation, offset by the R&D super-deduction. Terminal cap 15x FCF (not 20x): licensing-dependent, policy-exposed franchise with chronically single-digit-to-low-teens P/E history.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward mix blend, not a historical CAGR: innovative/exclusive products ~60% of directly-sold turnover growing ~20% (FY2025 +44%, H1 FY2026 +20%) plus a ~40% VBP-impacted legacy book now flat; H1 FY2026 turnover +12.5%. Historical CAGRs straddle the FY2023-24 VBP break (revenue 9,150 -> 7,469 -> 8,212) and are not a usable base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+6.0% / +9.5%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (-3.5% / +3.4%) and EPS (-22.6% / -9.7%): book value compounded through retained earnings and FVTOCI gains while the VBP reset and the FY2025 tax clawback cut earnings. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - licensing deposits for intangible assets (interest received is in investing and already outside reported FCF). Owner FCF (RMB m): FY2017 1,995; FY2018 1,698; FY2019 2,215; FY2020 2,351; FY2021 2,292; FY2022 3,010; FY2023 2,200; FY2024 813; FY2025 217. The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-58%) is far below the reported FCF CAGR (-41%): licensing reinvestment rose from 5.5% to 5.8% of revenue (10.4% in H1 FY2026) while OCF fell on VBP and a RMB650m FY2025 receivables build. SBC is immaterial (<0.4% of revenue) and does not drive the gap.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +11% (H1 actual +12.5%; H2 FY2025 comp is softer); innovative/exclusive engine ~20% on 60% of turnover against a flat legacy book gives ~10% blended, fading as newly launched products (Lumirix, Desidustat, Silevimig, Lucentis/Beovu) mature and NRDL price steps bite; 3% by FY2035 toward 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC, post-IFRS-16, ex non-operating income) 23.6% FY2025, ~27.4% H1 FY2026; FY2026 anchored 25.0% (H2 carries the R&D step-up), rising 50bp/yr to 27.0% as the higher-margin innovative mix outgrows the VBP book and R&D expense stabilises near 7% of revenue. Capped well below the pre-VBP ~40%.
base.capex_rationale: PPE ~0.5% + licensing deposits: FY2026 7.5% (H1 already RMB468m on the Novartis ophthalmology and Genrix deals), fading to 4.5% as the portfolio refresh normalises; terminal 5.0% total vs D&A 3.5% = ~1.5% of revenue net reinvestment funding 2.5% growth.
base.tax_rationale: 22% cash rate: PRC statutory 25%, FY2025 normalized ETR on operating profit ~20.5%, local concession lost (clawed back FY2025), 5-10% withholding on dividends repatriated to the Cayman parent, R&D super-deduction offsets.

scenario_narratives.base: The VBP reset is digested and the growth engine is the ~60% of turnover in innovative/exclusive products, compounding ~20% on new launches (Lumirix for vitiligo, Desidustat, Silevimig, in-licensed Lucentis/Beovu) while the legacy book holds flat under residual NRDL price steps. Blended revenue growth fades from ~11% to 3% over ten years. The mix shift lifts adjusted EBITDA margin from ~25% to 27% even as expensed R&D stays near 7% of revenue. In-licensing deposits stay a permanent reinvestment line, fading from ~7.5% to ~4.5% of revenue as the current deal wave is absorbed. Working capital remains a drag (receivable-heavy, payable-light). Dermavon spin-off and the Singapore/EM hub are treated as options, not modelled upside. The associate stakes and FVTPL portfolio are valued at book/haircut fair value in the bridge, not for any strategic premium.
scenario_narratives.bull: New launches ramp faster than the launch-year cadence suggests and the pipeline (6 NDAs under review, ~20 clinical programs) converts on schedule, keeping innovative-product growth above 25% for several years; VBP-exposed products stop declining; the out-of-hospital/DTP channels and the Singapore-hub emerging-market registrations add a second leg. Revenue compounds ~14% near term, fading to 4%. Operating leverage on the promotion platform plus a maturing R&D ratio lifts adjusted EBITDA margin to 30% -- still far below the pre-VBP 40%+. Licensing reinvestment eases to 4.5% of revenue as in-house programs replace bought-in rights, and the cash tax rate settles at 20% with better use of R&D incentives. Dermavon's separate listing and partial monetisation of the investment portfolio would be upside beyond this case.
scenario_narratives.bear: Another VBP or NRDL round reprices one of the key exclusive products (VELPHORO, Metoject, ILUMETRI) the way three products lost ~RMB1.7bn in 2023, one or more in-licensing partners renegotiates or walks at renewal, and a lead launch (Lumirix) under-delivers, so growth stalls near 2% after FY2027. To defend the portfolio the company keeps buying rights at 6-7% of revenue while expensed R&D stays elevated, so adjusted EBITDA margin slides to 20%. Receivables keep stretching (wc capture -45%), and a 24% cash tax rate reflects the loss of local concessions with no offset. A terminal growth of 1.5% and the 15x cap leave the company worth roughly its net cash plus investment portfolio plus a modest franchise -- below the current price. This case does not hit the zero-FCF floor; it is a value trap rather than a solvency event.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: the moat is contractual and time-limited, VBP/NRDL rounds are structural and recur annually, and the FY2025 tax clawback shows the regulatory earnings volatility is not confined to pricing. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- pipeline conversion, continued deal access against Hengrui/Sino Biopharm competition, and international execution -- while the base case already credits the launch wave now visible in H1 FY2026.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band collapsed: SBC is 0.35% of revenue, so street IV exceeds house IV by only ~HK$0.3/share and the current price lies far outside that band. The arithmetic band_position (~-1,960%) is meaningless and is reported as null per owner-fcf-adaptations (e); the price is below BOTH bases in every scenario except bull.

valuation_philosophy.summary: China Medical System is a specialty-pharma commercialisation platform whose economic capex is the stream of upfront/milestone payments for exclusive product rights, not property, plant and equipment. The valuation therefore charges licensing deposits as capex every year, strips all non-operating income (associates, FVTPL marks, interest) from the flows and adds the matching assets once in the bridge, discounts RMB flows at a CNY-built 9% cost of equity, and caps the terminal value at 15x owner FCF for a policy-exposed, licensing-dependent franchise. Roughly a third of the resulting value sits in the bridge (net cash plus the associate and investment portfolio); the operating franchise is valued on a ~15% terminal owner-FCF margin that equals today's normalized operating NOPAT margin -- i.e. no margin heroics, only the mix-driven recovery already visible in H1 FY2026.
key_risks_to_valuation: Bridge dependence: associates (RMB3.8bn at book) and FVTPL assets (RMB3.2bn, Level-3 management valuations, taken at 80%) are ~RMB2.8/share (~HK$3.3). A 50% haircut to the FVTPL book would cut every scenario by ~HK$0.6/share.
VBP/NRDL repricing of a key exclusive product -- the 2023 episode removed ~RMB1.7bn of revenue from three products in one year; the bear case models a repeat.
Licensing capex intensity: if the H1 FY2026 pace (10% of revenue) is the new normal rather than a deal-wave spike, owner FCF is ~RMB250-400m/yr lower than modelled through the mid-years.

Working-capital stretch: trade receivables rose RMB447m on RMB743m of revenue growth in FY2025; the model charges -35% capture, but continued DSO lengthening (or a collectability event on associate/Tibet Pharmaceutical receivables) would depress cash conversion further.
Tax: the FY2025 RMB278.8m clawback shows local incentives can be reversed retroactively; the 22% rate assumes no further surprises but no return of the concession either.
Currency: value is built in RMB and converted at 1.1721 CNY/HKD; a 5% RMB depreciation against the USD-pegged HKD lowers every HKD figure by ~5%.

Governance/complexity: HK+SGX listings, a pending Dermavon spin-off by distribution in specie, and a large discretionary investment portfolio dilute the link between operating cash flow and what reaches minority shareholders.
